name: Biblical Stewardship & Creation Care

objectives.text: Name ways people can take care of plants, animals, and the outdoors
Identify things in creation that people depend on for food, water, and shelter
Demonstrate a simple daily care routine for a classroom plant or animal
Explain the biblical idea that people are called to tend and keep the earth God made rather than use it carelessly
Distinguish renewable from nonrenewable resources and explain why each requires different care
Describe how wasting food, water, or soil affects people, animals, and the land
Explain what it means to be a steward of something entrusted to you and apply that idea to the use of land, water, and animals
Explain how farmers and ranchers care for soil, water, and livestock as part of producing food
Identify human activities that help or harm a local habitat and explain their effects on the plants and animals living there
Compare a use of natural resources that reflects responsible care with one that reflects waste or neglect
Plan a small conservation or service project that improves the school grounds or a local natural area
Summarize the relationship between natural resources, ecosystems, and human activity as the foundation for stewardship
Explain why preserving biodiversity is part of creation care and how it supports ecosystem function and resource availability
Illustrate stewardship of natural resources through a specific practice carried out in an SAE or FFA chapter activity
Demonstrate a resource management practice such as erosion control, habitat improvement, or water quality protection
Describe how technologies such as precision agriculture have changed the ability to use and care for natural resources
Assess how a specific agricultural or development activity affects the long-term availability of soil, water, or wildlife resources
Evaluate a real-world resource decision for whether it treats the earth as something to be cared for and passed on or something to be used up
Analyze how viewing the earth as a gift entrusted by God, as a mere commodity, or as something to be worshiped shapes how people use natural resources
Analyze how conservation practices such as cover crops, rotational grazing, or no-till sustain both farm productivity and long-term resource health
Develop a stewardship plan for a farm, woodlot, or SAE enterprise that sustains production while protecting soil, water, and wildlife
Justify a personal or community stewardship commitment that balances responsible use of natural resources with lasting care for creation

changes: Kept all six original objectives, rewording the grade 4 one to name the biblical tend-and-keep calling explicitly. Added early hands-on care and dependence on creation (grades 3), renewable versus nonrenewable resources and waste (grade 5), agricultural care of soil, water, and livestock (grade 6), local habitat impacts (grade 7), and a service project plan (grade 8). For grades 9 to 12 added AFNR-anchored competencies: human activity and ecosystems, biodiversity, stewardship in SAE and FFA, hands-on management practices, technology, impact assessment, worldview views of creation, conservation practices that sustain productivity, and a full stewardship plan. Laws, agencies, and economic policy content was left to Environmental Policy & Ethics, recreation to Outdoor Recreation & Safety, and careers to Careers in Natural Resources.
